title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Geometry
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: If the area of a regular hexagon is equal to the area of an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm, then the length, (in cm), of each side of the hexagon is
questions.explain:
Area of an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 12^2 = 36\sqrt{3}$ cm$^2$.
A regular hexagon is made up of 6 equilateral triangles. If its side is $a$, its area = $6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} a^2$.
Equating the areas: $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} a^2 = 36\sqrt{3}$
$a^2 = 36 \times \frac{2}{3} = 24$
$a = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}$ cm.

questions.q: Suppose the length of each side of a regular hexagon ABCDEF is 2 cm. If T is the mid point of CD, then the length of AT, in cm, is
questions.explain:
Let the center of the hexagon be at the origin $(0,0)$. By orienting the hexagon appropriately, coordinates for A can be $(0, 2)$, B $(\sqrt{3}, 1)$, C $(\sqrt{3}, -1)$, D $(0, -2)$.
Wait, an easier setup is placing A at the origin $(0,0)$ and extending the perimeter. 
Alternatively, use the law of cosines. In $\triangle ACD$, $AC = 2\sqrt{3}$. The interior angle of a regular hexagon is $120^\circ$. The angle $\angle ACD = 90^\circ$. 
Let's map it. Triangle AC is the diagonal across one angle, its length is $2\sqrt{3}$. Triangle ACD is a right triangle at C with legs AC $= 2\sqrt{3}$ and CD $= 2$. T is the midpoint of CD, so CT $= 1$.
In right $\triangle ACT$, $AT^2 = AC^2 + CT^2 = (2\sqrt{3})^2 + 1^2 = 12 + 1 = 13$.
$AT = \sqrt{13}$ cm.

questions.q: A circle of diameter 8 inches is inscribed in a triangle ABC where $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$. If $BC = 10$ inches then the area of the triangle in square inches is
questions.explain:
Let $BC = a = 10$, $AB = c$, and hypotenuse $AC = b$.
The inradius of a right-angled triangle is given by $r = \frac{a + c - b}{2}$.
Given diameter is 8, so $r = 4$.
$4 = \frac{10 + c - b}{2} \implies c - b = -2 \implies b - c = 2$.
By Pythagoras theorem: $b^2 - c^2 = a^2 = 10^2 = 100$.
Using difference of squares: $(b - c)(b + c) = 100$.
Substitute $b - c = 2 \implies 2(b + c) = 100 \implies b + c = 50$.
Adding $b - c = 2$ and $b + c = 50$, we get $2b = 52 \implies b = 26$.
Thus, $c = 24$.
The area of the right-angled triangle = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times c \times a = \frac{1}{2} \times 24 \times 10 = 120$ sq inches.
